dialect.detail: IBM Rational Developer for z/OS (RDz) test case, evidenced by .rdz.cbl extension and program-id DVZZMFT3 (DVZ prefix typical of IBM RDz test programs). Uses DB2 EXEC SQL ALTER SEQUENCE syntax.
evidence: ALTER SEQUENCE with DB2-style options (MINVALUE, MAXVALUE, CYCLE, CACHE, ORDER, RESTART, INCREMENT BY)

purpose.domain_detail: IBM RDz SQL parser/compiler test case for ALTER SEQUENCE statement variations
purpose.summary: This program is a test case for the IBM Rational Developer for z/OS SQL preprocessor or parser. It contains a single EXEC SQL block in the WORKING-STORAGE SECTION that exercises numerous variations of the ALTER SEQUENCE DDL statement (MINVALUE, MAXVALUE, RESTART, INCREMENT BY, CYCLE, CACHE, ORDER). The PROCEDURE DIVISION simply executes GOBACK.

notable_features: EXEC SQL with ALTER SEQUENCE DDL statements
Multiple ALTER SEQUENCE variants in a single EXEC SQL block
SQL embedded in WORKING-STORAGE SECTION (unusual placement)
No PIC clauses or host variables
verdict.notes: The .rdz.cbl extension strongly indicates IBM Rational Developer for z/OS. The program appears to be a parser/compiler regression test for ALTER SEQUENCE SQL syntax variations. Embedding EXEC SQL in WORKING-STORAGE is atypical for production code and reinforces the test-case interpretation. No host variables or actual DB2 runtime execution is expected.
